sentences.text: Dallasaurus is one of the smallest known mosasaurines, reaching approximately 1 meter in length.
Unlike giant mosasaurs like Tylosaurus and Mosasaurus, this creature was similar in size to its living relative, the Komodo dragon, measuring less than a meter long.

The genus name Dallasaurus honors Dallas County, the location where the fossils were discovered, while the species name turneri honors amateur collector Van Turner. Dallasaurus was described by Polcyn and Bell in 2005.
Fossils of Dallasaurus were found in the Arcadia Park Shale in Dallas County, Texas, near the contact with the Kamp Ranch Limestone.
The two known specimens were found approximately 100 meters apart at sites that were temporarily exposed during housing development excavations and have since been reburied by construction.

The holotype specimen consists of an incomplete skull and postcranial skeleton representing about 80 percent of the animal, while the second referred specimen lacks a skull and consists entirely of disarticulated postcranial remains.

Dallasaurus likely lived an amphibious lifestyle, as plesiopedal mosasauroids were capable of terrestrial locomotion unlike entirely aquatic hydropedal mosasaurs. It is thought that Dallasaurus led an amphibious lifestyle because its limbs allowed it to move on land while it could also swim.

Dallasaurus is a basal mosasauroid from the Upper Cretaceous of North America. Cladistic analysis places Dallasaurus within the subfamily Mosasaurinae and the family Mosasauridae, excluding it from the paraphyletic family Aigialosauridae. Dallasaurus belongs to the family Mosasauridae and is classified within the subfamily Mosasaurinae. A cladistic analysis by Bell and Polcyn in 2005 placed Dallasaurus within the subfamily Mosasaurinae and the family Mosasauridae. Dallasaurus is related to other derived mosasauroids such as Clidastes, Prognathodon, Mosasaurus, and Plotosaurus. Despite its plesiomorphic limb condition, Dallasaurus should not be placed in the paraphyletic family Aigialosauridae. The parent group of Dallasaurus is Mosasaurinae. Dallasaurus is classified in the class Reptilia.

Dallasaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Turonian age. Dallasaurus lived during the Upper Cretaceous. Dallasaurus lived during the Turonian stage, between 93.9 and 89.8 million years ago.

The popular press has described Dallasaurus as a "missing link" between fully aquatic mosasaurs and their terrestrial ancestors. Popular media has hailed Dallasaurus as a "missing link" connecting its terrestrial ancestors to fully aquatic mosasaurs.
